analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים, the third-person masculine singular verb identifies God as the one speaker addressing Noah and his sons.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים אֶל נֹחַ, אֶל introduces Noah as the person to whom God speaks. The parallel וְאֶל בָּנָיו adds his sons as further addressees.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: אֶל נֹחַ וְאֶל בָּנָיו means “to Noah and to his sons.” God addresses Noah by name, then includes his sons.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preposition אֶל is a separate word.

draft.change: Add Gen.9.8 as evidence for the existing addressee sense of אֶל at word index 0.
draft.definition: With a verb of speaking, אֶל introduces the addressee.
draft.evidence: In Gen.9.8, וְאֶל בָּנָיו adds Noah’s sons to the hearers already introduced by אֶל נֹחַ.

analysis.evidence: After וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים, “God said,” the parallel phrases אֶל נֹחַ וְאֶל בָּנָיו name the hearers, “to Noah and to his sons.” The repeated אֶל introduces the sons as fellow recipients of the same speech.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins two prepositional phrases. The preposition אֶל takes בָּנָיו, “his sons,” as its object.
analysis.sense: Marks the person or people addressed.
